newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Tractor sees strong tractor demand in China.
newsitem.headline: First Tractor sees strong tractor demand in China.

text.p: Chinese agricultural tractor maker First Tractor Co Ltd sees strong demand for the company's products and expects to benefit from Beijing's emphasis on developing China's agricultural industry .
First Tractor said in a statement on Tuesday that development of the agricultural industry was one of the top priorities of the Chinese government.
"The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies, which include lowering value-added tax on agricultural machinery," the company's chairman Yin Jia Xi said.
Policies also include provision of government subsidies for the purchase of agricultural machinery and the increase of loans to agricultural sector, Yin added.
First Tractor said earlier on Tuesday it is offering 300 million H-shares at HK$4.50 per share in a global offering.
H-shares are Chinese enterprise shares listed in Hong Kong.

Of the total, 255 million H shares will be earmarked for international placement, and 45 million shares will be offered for public subscription in Hong Kong. Dealing in the company's shares is expected to begin on June 23.
"As the nature of farming in China shifts from small-scale family operations to large-scale commercial operations, powerful agricultural tractors will be necessary," Yin said.
"The market for small to medium horsepower agricultural tractors will continue to grow in the short-term," he added.

First Tractor had said it would use the net proceeds of the approximately HK$1.29 billion to be raised from the new issue to finance expansion of its manufacturing capacity, repay debt and for working capital.
